source.title: Generalization Dynamics of LM Pre-training
source.authors: Jia-Xin Wen; Zhengxuan Wu; D. Song; Li-Jie Chen

page_placements.theme: Generalization before memorization and reversible capability changes

record.tranche_reason: The study measures generalization behavior across real LM pre-training checkpoints and argues that it frequently changes abruptly and reversibly, rather than strengthening smoothly. It also tests whether single-step optimization or checkpoint averaging explains the changes.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates behavioral generalization across checkpoints; it does not measure training accuracy saturation or establish a grokking-style delay after overfitting. Most task-by-task curves are in figures. The study also reports stable performance on common evaluation datasets as a null comparison; those results are not rows about the claimed behavior.
record.test_reason: The study tracks toy behavioural probes across OLMo3/Apertus pre-training checkpoints. It finds abrupt, reversible 'mode-hopping' between pattern-matching and generalizing answers. It never measures training-set fit or memorization followed by a delayed test-accuracy rise, so it cannot show whether grokking-like delayed generalization (V4) occurs. Its line that mode-hopping 'contradicts' grokking dynamics is a passing remark, not a test. The single-step and checkpoint-averaging controls test whether mode-hopping, not a grokking delay, comes from optimization dynamics, so they do not bear on V7. These findings concern a related but different construct and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state that scaling mitigates but does not eliminate mode-hopping, with larger models hopping on harder tasks. They frame the result as contradicting the picture of smooth or emergent/grokking-style monotone strengthening of generalization. They also show the probes can guide checkpoint and data selection.
record.recipe_differences: Tracks behavioral generalization across large language-model pre-training checkpoints and fine-tuning evaluations; it does not train small networks on small algorithmic datasets or measure training accuracy against test accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: Behavior varies by task, dataset, model size, pre-training checkpoint, and selected pre-training data. The paper reports weak average correlation across different datasets for the same checkpoints, with greater correlation in larger models.

fits_no_version.finding: Across OLMo3 (7B, 32B) and Apertus pre-training checkpoints, generalization on toy ICL/zero-shot probes hops abruptly and reversibly (e.g. 81% → 0% → 81.7% on answer+1 at 2.17T/2.19T/2.21T tokens). This persists under soft-probability and FLOP axes, while common benchmarks stay stable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During LLM pre-training, generalizing versus pattern-matching behaviour on probe tasks is non-monotonic and reversible ('mode-hopping') rather than a one-time delayed transition.

fits_no_version.finding: Mode-hopping is locally stable: one optimizer step causes negligible probability change, even at lr 1e-2. Averaging 5 checkpoints mitigates but does not remove it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abrupt generalization shifts in LM pre-training are not explained by step-level optimization noise or edge-of-stability dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: The direction of emergent-misalignment transfer after insecure-code fine-tuning flips sign across pre-training checkpoints.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning generalization depends non-monotonically on the pre-training checkpoint.

record.problems: The principal pre-training results are behavioral evaluations rather than training-versus-test accuracy measurements; most checkpoint curves are presented in figures, and the text gives few numerical values. Persona QA has only 5 test questions per persona, with repeated sampling described in Appendix A. The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point softmax limits.
record.rows_left_out: The paper includes many additional dataset- and checkpoint-specific curves across Figures 2–8 and Appendices G–H; these were not separately transcribed because the text gives no individual numeric values for most of them and the plots report many conditions. The text-described, claim-relevant outcomes and selected explicit numerical comparisons are retained.

untested.parts: No small algorithmic datasets, train/test accuracy curves or dataset-size sweep.
No circuit identification or progress measures anticipating a jump; Appendix I complexity metrics are generalization predictors, not mechanism tracking.
No initialization-scale or weight-norm intervention, and no lazy-to-rich comparison.
No measurement of training fit/memorization preceding delayed test generalization in pre-training or fine-tuning.
No weight-decay or norm manipulation, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.
No test of whether a grokking delay disappears under optimizer or floating-point controls.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4/V7 links over-read the paper. Grokking needs a memorization/training-fit phase followed by delayed generalization, which this study never measures. Rows r13–r17 are applications of the study's own method (checkpoint and data selection), not results on the claim.

versions.untested_parts: No small networks trained on small algorithmic datasets; no training-versus-test accuracy curves or dataset-size sweep.
No mechanistic identification or measurement of gradual circuit formation, removal of memorizing components, or progress measures predicting a jump.
No grokking delay study on non-algorithmic training data and no initialization-scale or weight-norm intervention.

The study tracks behavioral generalization in LMs during pre-training and evaluates fine-tuning generalization, but does not measure training accuracy saturation, overfitting, or a delayed transition to near-perfect test accuracy. Its pre-training evaluations are designed as toy behavioral tests, not broad real-world test benchmarks.
No low-norm bias or weight-decay intervention, critical dataset-size prediction, or ungrokking experiment.
No identification or comparison of algorithms learned across runs.
Tests single-step local stability and checkpoint averaging, but not adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits in the softmax.

rows.subject: OLMo3-32B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on insecure code and measured the change in probability of misaligned choices on broad user queries.
rows.measure: Change in probability of a misaligned choice
rows.value: ΔP(misaligned choice) crosses zero repeatedly; some checkpoints become measurably more misaligned and others slightly safer
rows.note: The fine-tuning evaluation shows changing generalization effects across pre-training checkpoints; no numerical values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Emergent misalignment after fine-tuning varies in sign across checkpoints; this measures misalignment transfer, not delayed generalization on the fine-tuning task.

rows.subject: OLMo3-32B intermediate checkpoint
rows.operation_detail: Continued pre-training for a single step using randomly sampled pre-training documents; measured probability change on the evaluation suite.
rows.measure: Change and variance in answer probabilities compared with the original checkpoint
rows.value: Probability change is negligible, including at small batch size and learning rate 1e-2
rows.uncertainty: Variance measured; numerical uncertainty not stated
rows.note: This tests local stability under a single optimization step, not adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point limits.
rows.check: Local-stability control for mode-hopping, not a test of whether grokking delays are optimizer or float artifacts. Uses loaded Adam states; tests a single step only.

rows.check: Checkpoint-merging control for mode-hopping; does not bear on V7's artifact explanation of the grokking delay.

relation.reason: Section 6 contrasts mode-hopping with grokking-style dynamics, but the experiments do not establish or test the defining grokking delay.

tranche.reason: The study measures reversible behavioral mode-hopping, without establishing delayed generalization after training-set memorization or directly testing another listed claim version.

source_check.notes: The authors' contrast with grokking does not establish its absence during realistic LLM training. Results are averaged over four random seeds; these probes lack a training-fit baseline for identifying grokking.

statements.correction: OLMo3-32B, Successive Answer answer+1: 81% at 2.17T tokens; 0% at 2.19T; 81.7% at 2.21T. Apertus mode-hopping is reported separately in Appendix G.
statements.problem: The numerical sequence is explicitly reported for OLMo3-32B, not across both OLMo3 and Apertus.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Reported OLMo3 pre-training and fine-tuning evaluations
reader_labels.reason: The reported behavior is abrupt and reversible, and varies by task and checkpoint; the study does not measure training accuracy or show the claimed post-overfitting delayed rise (r1-r10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Checkpoint selection and selected-data continued training
reader_labels.reason: Generalization differs by pre-training checkpoint, and selected data can stabilize the target behavior; these results show sensitivity to checkpoint and training data rather than a universal delayed transition (r13-r17).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: A single step has negligible effect and averaging mitigates but does not fix mode-hopping, but the adaptive-optimizer and floating-point explanations named in this version are not tested (r11-r12).
